issue.title: Targeted defect fixes for the prompt_prose wire, update races, Telegram transport, bundle caps, and triage conflicts
issue.description: Host-produced artifact-link origins, including prompt_prose, round-trip through the real sase_core_rs binding, and a contract test fails on any future origin drift. Jobs and launches that overlap a code swap defer and retry instead of failing, an update-overlap reproducer guards that behavior, and a prebuilt-artifact cache miss is a miss rather than a failure. Telegram falls back to plain text only on entity-parse errors, retries per chunk without resending delivered chunks, reports credential and network outages once per state transition, and runs its outbound job only on the sending machine. Every provider root bundle fits its declared max_bytes through compile-time compaction, with a doctor check and a just-check test that catch growth. bead_task_triage recovers from request_id_conflict by advancing the generation.

issue.title: Defer and retry scheduler jobs that overlap a code swap
issue.description: swap_chop_guards: the code-swap writer records a durable last-swap stamp. The chop runner does not start scripts while a writer is live, and it treats a missing script within a short post-swap grace as inhibited. A run that overlapped a swap and died of SIGBUS or a swap-skew import error is recorded as a skipped retry, not an error. Flip the chop xfails.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase swap_chop_guards as one work unit

issue.title: Defer and retry launches and finalizers that overlap a code swap
issue.description: swap_launch_guards: agent launches, bead work, and host finalizers that hit a missing binding or swap-skew import error during or just after a swap wait for it to end and retry. Long-lived processes stop mixing pre-swap and post-swap modules. Fix in-place native-code replacement only if the reproducer triggered SIGBUS. Flip the remaining xfails.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase swap_launch_guards as one work unit

issue.title: Treat a prebuilt Rust artifact cache miss as a miss, not a failure
issue.description: prebuild_miss: prebuild consume exits 0 and records hit:false with its reason on a cache miss. Dev-update reconcile records the step as a miss, then builds from source. The prebuild producer's writer probe also recognizes install.dev and install.pypi swaps.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase prebuild_miss as one work unit

issue.title: Fall back to plain text only on entity-parse errors and retry per chunk
issue.description: tg_transport: in sase-telegram, plain-text fallback fires only for an entity-parse BadRequest. Timeouts, network errors, rate limits, and credential errors reach the retry wrapper unchanged. Retries wrap each chunk, so delivered chunks are never resent, and the outbound job resumes a partly delivered notification at its first undelivered chunk.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase tg_transport as one work unit

issue.title: Collapse repeated Telegram credential and network failures into degraded states
issue.description: tg_degraded: outbound and receiver track a persisted credential_unavailable or network_degraded state. Each logs one line on entering a state, rate-limited summaries while degraded, and one line on recovery, with no tracebacks for transient errors. One SASE notice fires per transition. Credential lookups are negatively cached for a short window.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase tg_degraded as one work unit

issue.title: Compact oversize provider root bundles at compile time until they fit
issue.description: bundle_trim: when a provider declares max_bytes and the delivered bundle would exceed it, compile applies a deterministic compaction ladder. Step one drops summaries from superseded list-roster entries. Step two compacts whole list rosters, largest first. Bundles that already fit stay byte-identical, and no memory file changes.
issue.creation_reason: Epic plan plan:202611/defects_wire_swap_telegram_bundles_triage.md defines phase bundle_trim as one work unit

issue.title: Gate provider bundle sizes in sase doctor and just check
issue.description: bundle_gate: a sase doctor check renders every enabled project's root bundle for each provider that declares max_bytes. It errors over the cap and warns when compaction was needed. A just-check test keeps sase's own bundles under every cap without compaction. Update the instruction-bundle and Codex provider docs.

issue.title: Advance bead_task_triage's generation on request_id_conflict
issue.description: triage_conflict: when gate creation fails with request_id_conflict, bead_task_triage cancels any pending gate under the stale id and advances and persists the generation. It then recreates the gate in the same pass. Other failures keep the deterministic retry.

tg_transport landed in sase-telegram (uncommitted working tree in the linked checkout; host finalizer commits). telegram_client: plain-text fallback fires only for an entity-parse BadRequest (can't parse entities / message text); _get_bot() is outside the guarded block; TimedOut, NetworkError/Bad Gateway, RetryAfter, Forbidden, InvalidToken, TelegramCredentialError and non-parse BadRequests propagate unchanged. FINDINGS (swap_repro, item 5). Harness `tests/dev_update/_swap_harness.py` plus `test_swap_repro_{chops,imports,native}.py` drive the real chop runner (`run_configured_chop_once`), the real `code_swap_writer_lock` on a sandbox SASE_HOME, and real subprocesses (16 pass, 6 strict xfails, `raises=AssertionError`).

Modes that reproduce today (strict xfails):
- swap_chop_guards: (a') a job STARTS while a writer is live and runs (status success). (b) a script still missing just after the writer releases is a loud `missing_script`. (c) a job whose stub `sase_core_rs` vanishes mid-run fails exit 1 with "No module named 'sase_core_rs'", both with the writer live at exit and with the swap completed before exit. SIGBUS: a job holding a mapping of a file truncated in place under a live writer fails exit -7.
- swap_launch_guards: (d) a long-lived process that imported `launch_types` v1 lazily imports `launch_executor` v2 and fails "cannot import name 'BeforeSpawnCallback'". The xfail has a `LONG_LIVED_SWAP_GUARD = "module:factory"` seam (factory runs at process start and returns a should-restart predicate) for that phase to wire in.

Already covered (ordinary tests): (a) a script vanishing while the writer is live is an inhibited skip (ea7916d7a7); a guarded epic launch waits out the writer and execs against the restored binding; (f) a dev-update writer clears `wait_for_code_swap_readers` and takes the lock without waiting while a job is mid-run (jobs hold no reader lock), and a job that survives the overlap stays success.

Controls that must stay as they are: a missing script with no swap stays `missing_script`; a missing binding with no swap stays failure even though `capture_failure_facts` already marks that text `skew_suspect` (so overlap, not text, must decide); SIGBUS with no swap stays failure.

Evidence for swap_launch_guards' choice in (d): the mixed-version failure reproduces identically with in-place and with rename replacement, so atomic replacement does not help Python sources. Eager import at start keeps the process on v1 consistently, and a fresh process after the swap is v2-consistent. Both options work.

Native (e): in-place truncation SIGBUSes a process that mapped the file; a completed in-place rewrite changes bytes under the live mapping; rename, unlink-then-copy, and the real `prebuild_consumer._copy_atomic` keep the old bytes. Model: mapping a partially copied file past its EOF SIGBUSes (the glibc loader maps by ELF header sizes).

Versioned runtime instances are NOT required by this evidence. The narrower guards in the next two phases cover every reproduced mode. One gap is left: the maturin copy window for readers that no guard sees (see the PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP).

REAL INSTALL PATHS (item 3; read-only, plus a uv measurement in a temp UV_TOOL_DIR). No path rewrites a live inode in place.
- `uv tool install --force --reinstall` (`just install`, `just install-dev`) deletes and recreates the whole tool env, so every file gets a new inode. A 1-package temp env had its scripts and modules missing for about 0.46 s.
- Plain `uv tool install --editable` (`sase dev update`) uninstalls, then installs, each changed dist: new inodes, with a 1-2 ms gap.
- `maturin develop` (`rust-dev-install*`; maturin 1.15 logs "Removing previously built module") deletes the module, then copies it into a new inode at the final path. Confirmed live and read-only: on athena and apollo, long-lived processes still map older `sase_core_rs.abi3.so` inodes marked "(deleted)", while the current file is a newer inode.
- The prebuild consumer and the LSP install write a temp file and rename it. A git fast-forward unlinks and recreates files.

Field SIGBUS: all 6 SIGBUS exits in the last 7 days (athena tg_outbound, agent_auto_restart, sidecar_auto_sync; apollo comment_zombie_checks, stale_running_cleanup, pending_checks_poll) started while a writer was live, inside the dev update's "Rebuild Rust dev artifacts into the uv-tool venv" step. The athena runs lasted 0.45-0.78 s with no output; the apollo runs lasted 3-12 s. In-place rewrite is ruled out, so the likely mechanism is importing `sase_core_rs` mid-copy: a short new inode gives SIGBUS, and the gap gives ModuleNotFoundError. swap_chop_guards' "no starts during a swap" would have prevented all 6. swap_launch_guards item 4 (in-place rewrite) does not apply as written. The two missing-script events (Nov 16-17) predate ea7916d7a7, which covers that mode now.

MEASUREMENT before (item 6). Read-only, 2026-11-20 about 09:45 EST, last 7 days, within 120 s, using `tools/swap_overlap_census --tz America/New_York`. Sources: error digests, the error ring, retained run records, and launch_failures.jsonl. Windows: dev_update.jsonl records that changed something, plus install and update logs.
- athena: 62 update windows (59 dev_update, 2 install, 1 update). Digests: sigbus 3 (3 during), missing_binding 1 (1 during), missing_script 2 (2 during). Ring, runs, and launches: 0. Total: 6 events, all 6 near (all during a window).

payload.entry: IMPLEMENTED (swap_chop_guards). (1) Last-swap stamp: new src/sase/dev_update/code_swap_stamp.py writes ~/.sase/locks/code-swap-last.json {op, pid, started_at, completed_at, generation} atomically on every writer release, before the holder payload clears (so a prober always sees the live writer or the finished swap). It is written even when the swap body raised, never when the lock was refused or SASE_DISABLE_CODE_SWAP_LOCK=1. code_swap_writer_lock (both branches) and the stdlib installer SwapLock.release (tools/_sase_install_run.py, mirrored as LAST_SWAP_FILENAME / record_last_swap) share one generation counter, pinned by tests/sase_install/test_last_swap_stamp_parity.py. Readers treat a missing or corrupt stamp as no swap. (2) The chop runner no longer starts any script while a live writer holds the lock. (3) A missing script within CODE_SWAP_GRACE_SECONDS=120 of the last completed swap is an inhibited skip; after the window it is missing_script again. (4) Post-exit: a nonzero exit that overlapped a swap (writer live at exit, or last swap started<=finish and completed>start) and died of SIGBUS (-7) or matched runner_failure_facts skew patterns (via capture_failure_facts on the diagnostic output_excerpt) becomes status=skipped, skip_reason=inhibited, advances_cadence=False, checkpoint action_failed. It keeps exit_code and subprocess_diagnostic and has no error, so nothing reaches the error ring. Guards live in src/sase/axe/chop_swap_guard.py. (5) All 5 chop xfails in tests/dev_update/test_swap_repro_chops.py are flipped. The only remaining reproducer xfail is the swap_launch_guards (d) BeforeSpawnCallback one. payload.entry: FINDINGS (swap_launch_guards item 2). The field BeforeSpawnCallback failure (apollo launch_failures.jsonl err_261118_072052_6ce1b8, read-only) was raised by a TUI-submitted durable launch proc: `python3 -m sase run` (stage launch_proc, sidecar RUN_LAUNCH prompt for the tailnet-1a land). It booted before/during the 07:20 dev update (9.5 s swap), imported sase.agent.launch_executor_types at top level, and lazily imported launch_executor ~36 s later in launch_cwd_single (traceback lines show new source over old code objects). Athena shows the same class from the same process kind (agent_session_parallel_value, wire-is-stale, resolve_input_type binding missing: all `sase run` launch procs or older in-process launch_task rows). Approach chosen: approach 1 (record the swap generation at start; once it advances, stop in-process lazy work and restart cleanly), because the reproducer shows eager import only fixes the named modules while lazy imports are pervasive, and a fresh process is coherent. For CLI launches the restart is a wait-then-re-exec before any side effect; for scheduler routines it is a clean self-exit that the orchestrator respawns at once (closing the window before the installer or `sase update` restarts the scheduler). Finalizers use the eager-import option (preload), because a host completion cannot be re-exec mid-settlement. SIGBUS item 4: not applicable as written - swap_repro proved no real install path rewrites a live inode in place; the maturin copy-window fix is already sase-1tz.3.1.2 follow-up #4 (Justfile recipe work outside this phase).

(a) New light probe src/sase/core/code_swap_epoch.py (stdlib + sase.core.paths; sase.dev_update costs ~500 ms to import): snapshot_boot_swap_generation, code_swap_since_boot (same-state-root only), code_swap_writer_live, code_swap_in_play (live writer / since boot / within the 120 s grace), long_lived_swap_guard factory, wait_for_code_swap_writer.
